chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Ala' ibn Sa'id the freed slave of Al Sam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Marry the virgins, for they are the purest in speech, the best in morals, and the most fertile. Do you not know that on the Day of Judgment I will boast of you among the nations, even for a miscarriage? The child who died in the womb will be waiting at the Gate of Paradise. Allah, the Mighty and High, will say to it: Enter Paradise. It will say: No, not until my parents enter before me. Allah, the Mighty and High, will say to one of the angels: Bring me his parents. And they will be brought to Paradise, and He will say: This is due to My Mercy upon you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of marrying virgins and the fate of the unborn child in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Tawhid underscores the virtue of marrying virgins (abkar) for their natural purity and fertility, linking marital choice to spiritual merit. It illustrates the concept of 'muhabbat' (affection/intercession) where the unborn child (saqat) delays entry into Paradise until their parents arrive, showcasing Allah's justice and mercy in rewarding the deceased through their offspring.
